snip.t: In scurvy, there is defective formation of connective tissues and collagen in skin, cartilage, dentine, bone, and blood vessels, leading to their fragility.
C—false, soft/spongy bleeding gums are the classic sign of vitamin C (scurvy) deficiency, not B6.
Severe deficiency causes scurvy — manifesting as poor wound healing, bleeding gums, and easy bruising (not night blindness, which is a Vitamin A deficiency sign).

snip.t: Vitamin C deficiency → ↓ collagen hydroxylation → fragile capillaries → petechiae, poor wound healing, scurvy.
A deficiency of vitamin C results in the clinical presentation of scurvy.
